use: The finding being linked. Values are distinct per row in the profile, so a finding typically answers one catalogued question rather than several.

name: question_id
use: The catalogue question answered, referencing wa_obs_question_catalogue.obs_id. Only 31 questions appear despite 424 existing, and no FK enforces the reference.

name: coverage
use: How fully the finding answers the question. In practice the value tracks the finding's provenance rather than an independent judgement — 'direct' maps one-to-one onto the l2_api findings and 'full' onto the l2_mechanical ones — with 'answers', 'partial' and 'rollup' appearing only a handful of times.

name: created_at
use: When the link was made; formats are mixed between space-separated and ISO-8601 UTC timestamps.

name: delete_flagged
use: Soft-delete marker; effectively unused, with only a single row flagged.

name: id
use: Surrogate primary key. Table empty; never used.

name: finding_id
use: Intended to identify the revised finding and indexed for lookup, but no rows exist.

name: field
use: Intended to name the finding column that changed. Never populated.

name: value_from
use: Intended to hold the field's prior value. Never populated.

name: value_to
use: Intended to hold the field's new value. Never populated.

name: reason
use: Intended to record why the revision was made. Never populated.

name: justified_by_finding_id
use: Intended to cite another finding as the warrant for the revision. Never populated.

name: revised_at
use: Intended revision timestamp. Never populated.

name: revised_by
use: Intended actor who made the revision. Never populated.

name: id
use: Surrogate primary key for the link row.

name: finding_id
use: The finding the verse supports; 1,446 distinct findings are represented, several citing more than one verse.

name: verse_record_id
use: The resolved wa_verse_records row for the verse. 98% NULL — only the small SUPPORT set was ever resolved to a verse record, so the link is textual rather than relational for almost every row.

name: reference
use: The verse as written text (for example '1 Cor 11:25'). Eight rows hold an em dash instead of a reference, a placeholder standing where no verse was actually cited.

name: role
use: Whether the verse anchors the finding or merely supports it. Values are 'anchor' and 'SUPPORT' — uncontrolled, and inconsistently cased between the two batches that wrote them.

name: created_at
use: When the link was written; six distinct timestamps show the table is the product of a handful of batch runs, not incremental authoring.

name: delete_flagged
use: Soft-delete marker; ten rows are flagged, the rest live.

name: id
use: Surrogate primary key.

name: code
use: The characteristic's unique handle, composed as book-Strong's-word (for example 'psa-H0014-submit'); unique across all 1,634 rows.

name: name
use: The English reading word that keys the sense ('zeal', 'needy one'); 1,099 distinct names, so the same English word recurs against different lemmas.

name: aka
use: Declared but never populated: 100% NULL on all 1,634 rows. Carried over from the legacy registry shape, which did use it.

name: family
use: Groups the characteristic into one of 48 thematic families ('wisdom-folly-teaching', 'desire-longing-appetite', 'inner-seat-heart-soul-spirit'), with 61 parked in 'other-uncategorised'. Convention only, no constraint.

name: status
use: Maturity of the characteristic; every one of the 1,634 rows is 'surfaced' — none has advanced beyond first surfacing.

name: books
use: Declared but never populated: 100% NULL. Superseded by book_scope, which carries the numeric book id instead.

name: gist
use: Declared but never populated: 100% NULL. The legacy registry used this for the one-line law or summary.

name: colour_range
use: Declared but never populated: 100% NULL. In the legacy registry this held how a characteristic changes sense by object.

name: junctions
use: Declared but never populated: 100% NULL. Intended for links to neighbouring characteristics.

name: open_questions
use: Declared but never populated: 100% NULL.

name: discovery_doc
use: Declared but never populated: 100% NULL — these rows were generated by index build, not by discovery documents.

name: provenance
use: The build that produced the row; a single value, 'ib-char-index-v3-meaning-keyed-2026', across the whole table.

name: created_at
use: Compact UTC timestamp (YYYYMMDDThhmmssZ, not ISO-8601 with separators like the rest of the schema). Only two values: the 2026-07-11 Psalms build and the 2026-07-14 Proverbs build.

name: updated_at
use: Compact UTC timestamp of the last change; identical to created_at on every row — nothing has been edited since its build.

name: char_key
use: The meaning key in lemma:reading form ('H8668:victory'). 1,455 distinct over 1,634 rows, so the key is not unique — the same lemma-plus-reading recurs across the two books.

name: key_word
use: The reading word of the key; duplicates name on every row.

name: key_span_id
use: The specific span occurrence chosen to anchor this sense, unique per row, pointing at the verse-span layer.

name: operation
use: What the term does in context, phrased as a verbal action ('refuse to submit', 'be needy', 'be defended') — the movement the characteristic performs, which is the study's live analytical object.

name: ledger
use: A generated evidence summary line per characteristic, stating occurrence count, book, stems, ESV reading and attested gloss; unique on every row and effectively the row's audit record in prose.

name: instance_count
use: How many occurrences of this sense were found in the book. Heavily long-tailed: 1,115 of 1,634 senses occur exactly once.

name: book_scope
use: The book this characteristic was surfaced in, as a numeric book id: 19 (Psalms, 877 rows) and 20 (Proverbs, 757). Stored as TEXT though the values are integers.

name: stems
use: The Hebrew verbal stem(s) attested for this sense, comma-joined where several ('Piel, Qal'). NULL on 1,003 rows, principally the non-verbal terms.

name: morph_codes
use: The morphology code(s) attested for the sense (for example 'HVvv2fs'); NULL on 385 rows.

name: esv_words
use: The ESV rendering(s) of the term at its occurrences, the English evidence behind the meaning key; NULL on 22 rows.

name: lexical_gloss
use: The attested dictionary gloss for the lemma, distinct from the contextual reading. Only 552 distinct values across 1,634 rows, and at least one row carries an empty string rather than NULL.

name: read_sense_variants
use: The distinct readings observed across this sense's occurrences, pipe-separated with transliteration; near-unique per row and the record of internal sense variation.

name: cluster
use: The single primary M-code cluster this characteristic maps to; NULL on 1,009 of 1,634 rows, so most surfaced characteristics are not yet mapped into the cluster model.

name: cluster_all
use: All cluster mappings with their names ('M15(Wisdom)', 'T2(Supplementary)'), pipe-style multi-value text rather than a join; NULL on 948 rows.

name: id
use: Row number from the old registry, 1-29. Not declared as a primary key — the table has no PK at all.

name: code
use: The old-style characteristic handle, a concept slug ('fear-of-the-lord', 'being-known') rather than the live table's lemma-keyed code.

name: name
use: The characteristic's full name, often carrying a disjunction ('Forgiveness / confession vs concealment') that the meaning-keyed model splits apart.

name: aka
use: Alternate phrasings and sub-motifs, dot-separated — the richness that ib_characteristic declares in the same column but never populates.

name: family
use: One of five broad families: formation, godward, reflexive, experiential, speech-relational. Far coarser than the live table's 48 families.

name: status
use: Maturity: 15 surfaced, 10 developing, 4 established — a graded scale that the live table has collapsed to 'surfaced' for everything.

name: books
use: Which books evidenced the characteristic, as abbreviations ('Psa,Pro'); 27 of 29 span both.

name: gist
use: A one-sentence statement of the characteristic's core operation or law; authored, unique, and populated on all 29 rows.

name: colour_range
use: How the characteristic shifts sense according to its object or state, with verse citations — the record of a characteristic's internal range.

name: junctions
use: Semicolon-separated pointers to neighbouring characteristics this one connects with; the relational-web layer of the old model.

name: open_questions
use: The unresolved research questions raised by the characteristic, authored on every row.

name: discovery_doc
use: Path to the discovery document behind the characteristic; present on 10 of 29 rows.

name: provenance
use: A single value on every row: 'ib-characteristic-registry-v1-20260703'.

name: created_at
use: ISO-8601 UTC creation timestamp; a single 2026-07-03 value across all 29 rows.

name: updated_at
use: Identical to created_at on every row — the registry was never edited after its load.

name: char_key
use: 100% NULL — the meaning key did not exist in this model. Present only because the table shares the live table's column shape.

name: key_word
use: 100% NULL; unused in this model.

name: key_span_id
use: 100% NULL; unused in this model.

name: operation
use: 100% NULL. The equivalent content in this model lives in gist.

name: ledger
use: 100% NULL; unused in this model.

name: instance_count
use: 100% NULL — these characteristics were not counted per occurrence.

name: book_scope
use: 100% NULL; the equivalent content lives in books.

name: id
use: Surrogate primary key; the minimum observed value is 39, so earlier rows were deleted.

name: operation
use: The inner-being operation observed, as a concept slug: 'heart' (20), 'ruthlessness' (17), 'dominion', 'fear-of-god', 'enslavement' and three others. Uncontrolled.

name: dimension
use: Which analytical dimension the observation belongs to, in the D-code scheme (D1..D13). All 13 appear; note the reset since dropped D10, D12 and D13, which are present here — legacy dimension codes.

name: narrative
use: The observation itself in prose — what the verse shows for this dimension. Some narratives explicitly correct the source verse-read finding, so this column also carries error notes.

name: term_anchor
use: The Strong's number the observation hangs on (H6531, H3372, G2588); 16 distinct anchors across the 81 rows.

name: origin_verse
use: The human-readable reference of the verse the observation came from; only 9 verses generated the whole table.

name: origin_verse_id
use: The numeric verse id for origin_verse; consistent with it, 9 distinct values.

name: reconsider_at
use: Free-text pointer to where the observation should be revisited — other verses, or a class of terms. Three rows carry a literal '-' meaning nothing to revisit.

name: status
use: Where the observation stands: resolved (56), needs-corroboration (15), open (8), silent (2).

name: provenance
use: How the observation arose: 'mechanical' (21), 'researcher+fan-out' (19), 'researcher' (11), 'convergence' (9), 'digested' and others — the distinction between machine-derived and researcher-authored evidence.

name: basis
use: The specific evidential warrant for the observation, for example a unit reading, a cited verse, or a witness count.

name: raw_file
use: The fan-out markdown document the observation was digested from; 8 files behind all 81 rows.

name: created
use: Creation timestamp, defaulting to datetime('now') and therefore in SQLite's space-separated form rather than the ISO-8601 Z form used across the rest of the schema. Only 3 distinct values.

name: strongs_number
use: The lemma being classified, H/G plus four zero-padded digits, and the primary key — one classification per Strong's.

name: faculty
use: The faculty or faculties the lemma engages, as a comma-joined list (e.g. 'affect,volition'). 815 of 1,717 rows hold an empty string rather than NULL, meaning the run examined the lemma and assigned no faculty; affect is the commonest positive value at 432. Uncontrolled — 36 distinct values with no constraint behind them.

name: basis
use: Free-text justification for the faculty call, typically the gloss plus a short reading of its sense (e.g. 'zealot/zealous — one characterised by burning eager devotion'). Near-unique per row (1,680 distinct of 1,717), so it is genuine per-lemma reasoning rather than boilerplate.

name: confidence
use: How firm the faculty call is. Recorded as four values where three were intended: 'high' (882), 'low' (235) and the medium band split across both 'med' (366) and 'medium' (234) — an unenforced vocabulary that must be normalised before the column is aggregated.

name: model_version
use: Identifier of the classifier that produced the row; uniformly 'faculty-map-v1-20260624' across every row, confirming a single unrevised generation.

name: created_at
use: When the row was written; identical for all 1,717 rows (2026-06-24 12:37:16), so it timestamps the run, not the row.

name: strong
use: The Strong's number, H/G plus four zero-padded digits, and the primary key — one row per Strong's, with no duplicates across the 11,666 rows.

name: original_unicode
use: The lemma in its own script, Hebrew or Greek (e.g. Ῥώμη, 'Rome'). 11,114 distinct values against 11,666 rows, so a few hundred Strong's entries share a surface form.

name: transliteration
use: Romanised form of the lemma; a reading aid that should never be cited without the gloss beside it.

name: gloss
use: Short English sense of the entry. Only 7,318 distinct values over 11,666 rows — common glosses are shared by many Strong's numbers, so the gloss alone does not identify an entry.

name: medium_def
use: The fuller STEP definition: the substantive lexical content of the row, running from a one-line sense to multi-hundred-character discussions with stem breakdowns and classical notes.

name: language
use: Language of the entry: Hebrew (7,027), Greek (4,638) and a single Aramaic row. Uncontrolled, and clearly not a real Aramaic classification — the one Aramaic row is the hand-added entry noted in source, so Aramaic lemmas otherwise sit under Hebrew here.

name: occurrence_count
use: How often the lemma occurs in the biblical corpus per STEP. Capped, not exact at the top end: five entries (including G0846 'it/s/he' and G2532 'and') sit at exactly 10000, which is a ceiling rather than a count. Zero is a legitimate value for entries with no attested occurrence.

name: source
use: Where the row came from: 'STEP' for all but one entry, the exception being a manually added Aramaic lemma that STEP returned empty.

name: fetched_at
use: When the entry was retrieved. Effectively a single bulk timestamp of 2026-06-16 for the whole table, plus the one manual row added on 2026-06-26.

name: id
use: Surrogate key for the cross-reference row.

name: mti_term_id
use: The term being cross-referenced, pointing to mti_terms.id; cascades on delete of the term. 279 distinct terms appear, so most cross-referenced terms have only one or two referring registries.

name: registry
use: Registry number of the referring English word, held as text (e.g. '178'). Part of the uniqueness key with mti_term_id, word and part.

name: registry_fk
use: Foreign key to word_registry.id for the referring word. Unlike the equivalent column on mti_terms this one is fully populated, and its 109 distinct values match registry exactly.

name: word
use: The referring English registry word (e.g. 'wrath'), denormalised beside registry; the two columns have identical cardinality, so this is a readability copy.

name: part
use: Which part of a split registry does the referring, where the English word was divided for processing. Set on only 17 rows and written inconsistently as both bare digits and 'Part3'.

name: word_data_reference
use: Pointer to the source Word_Data record that evidenced this cross-reference. Set on only 16 rows, so provenance for this table is effectively absent.

name: mti_term_id
use: The flagged term, half of the composite primary key with flag_id. 785 distinct terms carry flags, so most flagged terms hold a single flag.

name: flag_id
use: The flag type applied, pointing to phase2_flag_types.id. Only four types are used here: 1 GOD_AS_SUBJECT (584), 3 SOMATIC_INNER_LINK (410), 13 THEOLOGICAL_ANCHOR (9) and 4 BODY_INNER_EXPRESSION (2).

name: id
use: Surrogate primary key; maximum id 1,247 against 1,196 rows, so some placements were hard-deleted.

name: mti_term_id
use: The term being placed; 740 distinct terms, several placed into more than one sub-group.

name: cluster_subgroup_id
use: The sub-group the term is placed into; 160 sub-groups have members, the busiest holding 35 terms.

name: placement_note
use: Why the term sits here, citing the routing directive and marking the placement '[primary]' or '[secondary]' — this text is the only record of primary-versus-secondary status. 243 rows read 'M46 backfill from mti_terms.cluster_subgroup_id', marking the migration off the old single-valued column.

name: delete_flagged
use: Soft-delete marker; 173 of 1,196 placements retired and retained.

name: created_at
use: ISO-8601 UTC creation timestamp, in 27 directive-sized batches.

name: last_updated_date
use: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the last change to the placement.

name: id
use: Surrogate key for the term record; the value referenced as mti_term_id throughout the finding, verse-context and cluster layers.

name: strongs_number
use: The term's Strong's identifier, normally H/G plus four zero-padded digits (e.g. H7965), sometimes with a sub-entry suffix letter. Not clean: six rows hold placeholders such as 'PENDING-135-metameleia' or 'G_PENDING_epelpizo' for terms onboarded before a Strong's was resolved, and one row carries the unpadded 'G194'.

name: transliteration
use: Romanised form of the lemma, used to name the term in prose and reports. Never authoritative on its own — always read with the gloss; a few rows hold only whitespace.

name: gloss
use: Short English sense of the term (e.g. 'zealot'), the working label used when the term is named in analysis. Some values carry a leading space, and proper nouns such as ' Philippi' show that the intake was not filtered to inner-being vocabulary.

name: language
use: Source language of the term: Hebrew (5,457), Greek (2,281) or Aramaic (123). Convention only — no CHECK constraint enforces the three values.

name: owning_registry
use: The registry number of the English word that is this term's canonical home, held as text (e.g. '187'). Legacy text pointer superseded by owning_registry_fk but still the better-populated of the two — only 8 rows are null.

name: owning_registry_fk
use: Proper foreign key to word_registry.id for the owning English word. Populated on only 4,336 of 7,861 rows: 3,522 rows carry an owning_registry text value with no matching FK, so this column is an incomplete migration of that pointer and must not be treated as the sole ownership signal.

name: owning_word
use: The English registry word that owns the term, denormalised alongside owning_registry for readability.

name: owning_part
use: Which part of a split registry owns the term, where a large English word was divided for processing. Populated on only 350 rows and inconsistently written — both 'Part1' and '1' forms are in use, with no constraint to reconcile them.

name: word_data_reference
use: Text pointer to the Word_Data source record the term was extracted from. Populated on 1,399 rows only; a sparse provenance trail from the early STEP intake.

name: word_data_ref_fk
use: Integer form of word_data_reference, populated on exactly the same 1,399 rows and carrying the same values; a redundant typed copy of the text pointer.

name: status
use: Disposition of the term after extraction and triage: 'extracted' (2,572) and 'delete' (2,570) dominate, with 'extracted_thin' for sparse terms, 'extracted_theological_anchor' for deferred anchor terms, plus 'excluded' and 'candidate_delete'. Uncontrolled vocabulary with 11 distinct values and 2,276 rows left null, so status is not a reliable filter on its own.

name: exclusion_reason
use: Free-text justification, written at triage, for why a term was excluded or deleted — typically citing the verse evidence checked (e.g. root bleed, place name, no fear content). Present on 1,124 rows, i.e. a minority of the terms actually flagged out.

name: extraction_date
use: Date the term was pulled from STEP. Almost entirely March 2026 (3,536 rows on 2026-03-28 alone), confirming that mti_terms is a one-off bulk intake rather than a continuously grown table.

name: strongs_reconciled
use: 1 where the term's Strong's number was checked against the source and confirmed, otherwise 0. Only 294 rows are marked reconciled, so the flag records a small verification exercise rather than the table's general state.

name: anchor_note
use: Free-text note on terms treated as theological or framework anchors, recording the primary anchor verses or the onboarding gate that introduced the term. Present on 187 rows; 160 of those are the terse marker 'gate1-onboard-2026' rather than substantive prose.

name: last_changed
use: Timestamp of the last write to the row, spanning March to July 2026. Format is not consistent — early rows use space-separated local form ('2026-03-16 10:34:12'), later rows ISO-8601 UTC with a Z suffix.

name: delete_flagged
use: Soft-delete marker; 1 means the term is out of scope and 0 means live. The majority of the table (5,131 of 7,861) is flagged out, so any query over mti_terms must filter on this or it reads the discard pile.

name: vc_status
use: Verse Context progress for the term: 'not_done' (7,009), 'vc_completed' (761) or 'to_revise' (91). Defaults to 'not_done', so the large not_done count includes terms never worked as well as terms genuinely outstanding.

name: vc_instruction_version
use: Which instruction document version governed the term's Verse Context pass, recorded for provenance. Set on 680 rows and mixed in form — some values are document filenames, some bare names, one is literally 'unknown'.

name: vc_status_updated_at
use: Timestamp at which vc_status last moved. Populated on 851 rows, broadly matching the count of terms that ever left 'not_done'.

name: vc_status_note
use: Explanation of a vc_status change, present on 212 rows. Dominated by two machine-written reasons — an M37 backfill and a stale-value sync by validate_cluster_completion — so it mostly records automated corrections rather than researcher decisions.

name: md_version
use: Revision counter for the term's metadata, incremented on rewrite; 7,220 rows are still at the initial 1, and the highest observed is 5.

name: cluster_code
use: The M-code cluster the term belongs to (e.g. M01, M15), or 'T2' for the qualifier collection which is the single largest group at 1,301 rows. Null on 3,164 rows, and uncontrolled — no FK to the cluster table backs the 47 distinct codes.

name: id
use: Surrogate primary key; the target of verse.passage_id. The range runs to 4,401 against 4,296 rows, so about 100 passages have been deleted outright.

name: ref
use: The passage's human reference range, e.g. '1Ch 10:12-14'; unique across the table.

name: anchor_verse_id
use: The verse.id of the passage's first verse — the anchor at which term-driven processing begins. Its range reaches 23,984, exceeding some other tables' verse_id ceilings.

name: book_id
use: Canonical book number; Proverbs (20) has by far the most passages at 701, reflecting its verse-by-verse structure.

name: start_chapter
use: Chapter of the first verse. Identical to end_chapter on every row.

name: start_verse
use: Verse number of the first verse; 684 passages start at verse 1.

name: end_chapter
use: Chapter of the last verse — identical to start_chapter on all 4,296 rows, so it carries no information beyond start_chapter.

name: end_verse
use: Verse number of the last verse in the run.

name: verse_count
use: Number of verses in the passage, 1..39; the commonest are 2 (946) and 1 (642), so passages are typically very short.

name: source
use: How the passage was derived: 'consecutive' (3,579, the standard maximal-run rule), 'passage-build-2026' (701, all Proverbs) and 'single-verse-emergent-char-2026' (16). Convention only, no CHECK.

name: review_flag
use: Present on only the 16 single-verse emergent passages, all holding the string '0'. The declared type is TEXT but the content is a numeric flag, and with a single value it currently marks nothing.

name: notes
use: Present on only the same 16 rows, all with the identical text 'single-verse passage: isolated emergent characteristic, no adjacent char-verse' — a rationale for the exception, not a per-row note.

name: created_at
use: Creation timestamp with only three distinct values, each corresponding exactly to one of the three source campaigns.

name: id
use: Surrogate key for the flag type, 1-25.

name: flag_code
use: The flag's code, e.g. 'ARAMAIC_FORM', 'BODY_INNER_EXPRESSION', 'CAUSATIVE_OF_INNER_STATE', 'CROSS_TESTAMENT_SHIFT'. Unique, and the value referenced when a flag is raised.

name: description
use: The prose criterion for raising the flag, e.g. 'Fewer than 5 verse records or very low occurrence count; dataset too thin for confident Session B analysis'. Populated for all 25 and the only statement of what each code means.

name: id
use: Surrogate primary key for the prose section.

name: registry_id
use: The word_registry entry the section is about, where word-scoped. 15% populated (141/949) -- most sections are chapter- or cluster-scoped rather than word-scoped. Citation column (researcher, 2026-08-24): belongs in a future index table (book 5, Concordance), not directly on prose_section -- not acted on now, Concordance is out of scope for this build; likely to become redundant once that index table exists.

name: section_type_id
use: The kind of section, referencing prose_section_type. Heavily skewed — one type (lexical prose at chapter level) accounts for roughly half of all rows.

name: heading
use: The section's title, typically naming the scripture unit and the reading performed (for example 'Amo 1 - inner-being reading'). Not unique: some headings repeat across versions.

name: body
use: The prose itself — the actual authored text, often several thousand characters of markdown. This is the payload the whole table exists to hold and the content mirrored into the FTS index.

name: word_count
use: Cached length of body in words. Some rows record 0 despite holding text, so the count is not reliably maintained; the maximum (over 74,000) shows a few sections are book-length.

name: status
use: Editorial state, CHECK-constrained to draft, in_review, approved or archived. The great majority are approved; 'in_review' is permitted but never used.

name: version
use: A literal pointer to record_change_log.id -- the log row describing this section's own most recent change -- not an incrementing per-item counter. Corrected 2026-08-24 (escalation #836); prior mixed-type legacy values ('1_0'/'v1' strings) were resolved by the migration, every row now carries a fresh pointer.

name: supersedes_id
use: The earlier prose_section this row replaces. Present on 90 rows, forming a self-referential revision chain within the table.

name: superseded_by_id
use: The inverse pointer to the row that replaced this one, maintained symmetrically with supersedes_id on the same 90 rows.

name: author
use: Who wrote the section, CHECK-constrained to claude_ai, claude_code or researcher. The distribution is the notable thing: only one row in 1,039 is researcher-authored.

name: created_at
use: When the section was written, in ISO-8601 UTC. This column is consistently formatted, unlike its equivalents in the finding tables.

name: approved_at
use: When the section was approved. 87% NULL even though 922 rows are marked approved, so the approval timestamp was not kept in step with the status column.

name: approved_by
use: The approver — either claude_code or the value 'manual_backfill', which records that approval was applied retrospectively rather than by an actual reviewer. Null on most approved rows.

name: metadata_json
use: A JSON blob of scope and provenance for the section: book, chapter and verse list for chapter readings, or term, cluster_code, source and verses for term-scoped prose. Structure varies by section type and is not schema-enforced.

name: source_file
use: The markdown file the prose was ingested from, recording the path or filename it came in on. Near-universally populated, showing the store was built by importing files rather than authoring in place.

name: delete_flagged
use: Soft-delete marker; 59 sections are flagged out.

name: cluster_code
use: The M-code cluster the section belongs to, where cluster-scoped. 18% populated (175/949), free text, no FK to cluster (0 live orphans, checked). Citation column (researcher, 2026-08-24): belongs in a future index table (book 5, Concordance), same reasoning as registry_id -- not hardened with an FK now, not acted on now (escalation #832).

name: characteristic_id
use: The characteristic the section discusses, where characteristic-scoped. 13% populated (124/949). Citation column (researcher, 2026-08-24): belongs in a future index table (book 5, Concordance), same reasoning as registry_id/cluster_code -- not acted on now.

name: cluster_subgroup_id
use: Declared and indexed to scope a section to a cluster subgroup. 100% NULL -- never used. Citation column (researcher, 2026-08-24): belongs in a future index table (book 5, Concordance), same reasoning as its siblings -- not dropped now, not acted on now (escalation #832).

name: prose_section_id
use: Intended to identify the prose section, with an FK to prose_section. Never populated.

name: dimension_id
use: Intended to identify the dimension discussed. Never populated, and notably it carries no FK, so the target table was never even named.

name: link_type
use: Intended to qualify how the section relates to the dimension, defaulting to 'discusses'. Never populated, so no other link type is attested.

name: created_at
use: Intended insertion timestamp, defaulting to datetime('now'). Never populated.

name: prose_section_id

name: source
use: 'STEP' on every row — the table has one provenance, so the column currently distinguishes nothing.

name: fetched_at
use: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the STEP fetch; values run 2026-06-16 to 2026-07-05, matching the verse table's build window.

name: verse_id
use: The verse whose raw fetch this is; primary key and FK to verse, one row per verse with no gaps.

name: html
use: The unparsed STEP passage HTML for the verse, roughly 1kB+ per row. It is the provenance record for verse_morphology and is not intended to be read structurally in SQL.

name: fetched_at
use: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the fetch, spanning 2026-06-16 to 2026-07-05 in step with verse.created_at.

name: id
use: Surrogate primary key for the span row (not the same key space as verse_morphology.id despite the copy relationship).

name: verse_id
use: The verse the span sits in; the main lookup key. No FK is declared even though verse_morphology declares one.

name: reference
use: The verse reference, denormalised from verse for direct readability without a join.

name: word_index
use: The word's position in the verse, copied from verse_morphology.

name: surface
use: The surface word form, copied from verse_morphology; empty strings occur.

name: pos

name: morph_code

name: stem
use: Hebrew verbal stem copied from verse_morphology; empty string for non-verbs.

name: language
use: 'Hebrew', 'Greek', 'Aramaic' or 'Unknown', copied from verse_morphology.

name: strongs
use: The raw Strong's tag(s) copied from verse_morphology.

name: primary_strong
use: The resolved head Strong's number; indexed with verse_id, making (verse_id, primary_strong) the intended access path for finding a term's spans in a verse.

name: source
use: 'verse_morphology' on all rows — an explicit statement that this table is a derived copy of that one.

name: built_at
use: Timestamp of the row's build, spanning 2026-06-26 to 2026-07-05; unlike the coverage snapshots this table has been rebuilt incrementally.

name: role
use: The analytical role the span plays in the inner-being model: chiefly 'standalone' (63,719), 'characteristic' (13,514), 'process-qualifier' (7,155) and 'qualifier' (3,168), with a long tail of book-specific values such as 'ritual-mechanical' and 'mistag-not-ib'. Only 27% of spans have a role; the vocabulary is convention with no CHECK, and the tail suggests ad-hoc additions.

name: role_provenance

name: role_set_at
use: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp the role was set, 2026-07-07 to 2026-07-14 — role assignment is recent and ongoing.

name: role_source_ve_id

name: char_candidate
use: 1 marks the span as a candidate inner-being characteristic (30,882 rows); a single row holds 0 and the rest are NULL, so this is effectively a set-membership marker where NULL means 'not a candidate'. name: char_candidate_tag

name: characteristic
use: The free-text characteristic name attached to the span, keyed on meaning-in-context and often quoting the verse itself (e.g. 'your hand was heavy on me'). Populated on only about 1% of spans.

name: ib_char_id
use: The ib_characteristic this span resolves to — the structured counterpart of the characteristic text column, and populated on exactly the same rows.

name: cluster

name: verse_id
use: The verse containing the term; 23,405 distinct verses in the sample, and its ceiling of 23,593 matches the coverage snapshots rather than the full 25,634-verse master, suggesting it was built in the same earlier campaign.

name: primary_strong
use: The resolved head Strong's number present in that verse; indexed, and the point of the table.

name: id

name: item_id

name: addendum_group

name: rule_id

name: researcher_comment

name: created_at

name: last_modified

name: set_aside_count

name: total_verse_count

name: delete_flagged
use: Soft-delete marker; set on 29 entries.

name: dimension_confidence

name: manual_override
use: Marks the 190 entries where the researcher overrode the automated assignment.

name: notes
use: Free-prose justification for the assignment, present on about 40 per cent of entries; often records that an automated label was corrected and why.

name: last_modified
use: When the entry was last written. Confined to April and early May 2026 and recorded in three inconsistent formats (bare date, ISO without zone, ISO with Z).

name: dominant_subject
use: Who the group's verses are principally about: HUMAN (969), GOD, NONE, OTHER_HUMAN, UNSEEN. NULL on 2,321 rows, so it was only ever filled in for a minority. Uncontrolled vocabulary.

name: id

name: filename

name: word_registry_fk

name: word

name: part_number

name: total_parts

name: schema_version

name: phase

name: produced_date
use: The date the file was produced, ISO date only. 141 of 308 rows share 2026-03-18, the date of the bulk gap-fill.

name: source_file
use: The upstream document the data was taken from, e.g. 'word_fear.md', '200_energy_step_data_20260328.json'. NULL in 251 of 308 rows, so upstream provenance is recorded for only a fifth of entries.

name: translation_used

name: specification

name: revision_note

name: source_list

name: category

name: testament_coverage

name: last_changed
use: When the entry was last written, defaulting to datetime('now'). DEFECT of format: values here are space-separated ('2026-03-16 11:32:38') rather than the ISO-8601 T-separated form used across the rest of the schema, because the default calls datetime() rather than strftime().

use: Surrogate key for the pattern, 1-23.

name: pattern_code

name: deprecated

name: deprecation_note
use: Intended to explain a retirement, but NULL in all 23 rows.

name: created_at
use: When the pattern was registered. Identical ('2026-04-20T15:55:54') across all 23 rows — one bulk load.

name: last_modified

name: id
use: Surrogate primary key, also referenced by wa_prose_section_citations.cited_qa_link_id.

name: finding_id
use: The Session B finding being mapped, referencing wa_session_b_findings. Null on 743 rows — these are the 'no_finding'/'not_applicable' rows that record a question was considered but nothing answered it, which is itself the evidence.

name: mapped_date

name: validated_date

name: validated_by
use: Which analytical pass validated the mapping — a first-tier or second-tier Claude AI run. Null on the 488 rows marked 'validated', which is the inverse of what the name implies.

name: session_b_note
use: DEPRECATED (2026-08-29): the substantive finding write-up, but duplicated verbatim across every (finding_id, question_id) pairing it applies to (only 3,232 distinct texts across 6,199 rows) -- a normalisation violation, not a real per-row fact. use: Soft-delete marker; 414 mappings are flagged out.

name: finding_id
use: The Session B finding, referencing wa_session_b_findings. Only 49 distinct findings appear, each linked to up to fourteen entities.

name: entity_strongs

name: raised_date
use: When the link was made. Only three distinct timestamps, confirming three batch runs produced the entire table.

name: delete_flagged
use: Soft-delete marker; never used — all rows remain live.

name: id
use: Surrogate primary key for the link row.

name: flag_type_id
use: The quality flag type, referencing wa_quality_flag_types. Only four types participate, each triggering two to four questions.

name: question_id

name: context_note

name: active

name: created_at
use: Insertion timestamp. A single value across all twelve rows — the whole table was seeded at once.

name: id
use: Surrogate key for the pattern, 1-11.

name: pattern_code

use: Which column the identifier populates, e.g. 'wa_session_research_flags.flag_label', 'verse_context_group.group_code'. Given as a dotted string, so it is readable but not a checkable reference.

name: description

name: governing_instruction
use: Which document defines the format. Notable that two rows cite only 'historical convention' — an admission that the format has no governing document.

name: deprecated

name: deprecation_note
use: Intended to explain a retirement, but NULL in all 11 rows.

name: created_at
use: When the format was registered. Identical ('2026-04-20T15:55:54') across all 11 rows — the same bulk load that filled wa_file_name_pattern.

name: last_modified

name: id
use: Surrogate key for the LSJ parse record.

name: term_inv_id
use: The inventory term parsed, pointing to wa_term_inventory.id and unique — one LSJ parse per term.

name: raw_lsj
use: The LSJ entry as retrieved, unedited, complete with the lexicon's own citation markers ([Refs 8th c.BC+]) and dialect notes. The source text the other columns are derived from.

name: lsj_gloss
use: The classical sense extracted from the entry — e.g. for πλοῦτος (ploutos), 'wealth, riches'. In practice it is a truncation of raw_lsj rather than a clean gloss: the values still carry the lexicon's citation apparatus, so the extraction did not do what the column name promises.

name: lsj_domains
use: JSON array of usage domains detected in the entry. The parse has not worked: five of the seven populated rows hold just ['Refs'], which is the lexicon's citation marker mistaken for a domain, not a real domain. Only the ['NT'] row is meaningful.

name: lsj_philosophical_note
use: Intended to capture the entry's philosophical usage. Populated on one row only, and with the fragment 'Plut' — a truncated reference to Plutarch, not a note. No usable data.

name: lsj_etymology_note
use: Intended to capture the entry's etymological content. Populated on two rows, both holding Greek phrase fragments about deriving wealth from a source rather than etymology proper — the extraction has misfired.

name: lsj_cognate_forms
use: Declared to hold the entry's cognate forms, but NULL on all 9 rows — never populated.

name: parsed_at
use: When the LSJ entry was parsed: 7 rows in one run on 2026-05-14, plus two isolated rows from March 2026.

name: parse_version
use: Version of the LSJ parser; uniformly '1.0.0' across all 9 rows.

name: id
use: Surrogate key for the parse record; referenced as parsed_meaning_id by wa_meaning_sense and wa_meaning_stem, and mirrored back onto wa_term_inventory.parsed_meaning_id.

name: term_inv_id
use: The inventory term whose meaning was parsed, pointing to wa_term_inventory.id. Unique across the table — exactly one parse per term.

name: strongs_number
use: Declared NOT NULL but functionally empty: 7,736 of 7,748 rows hold an empty string, and only 12 carry a real Strong's. The term's Strong's must be read from wa_term_inventory instead.

name: language
use: Nominally the language of the parsed term, and demonstrably wrong. Only the 9 rows with a real Strong's are correctly marked Greek; 'Hebrew' is written by default on everything else, so 2,199 Greek terms and 187 Aramaic terms are mislabelled Hebrew — 31 per cent of the table. Do not use this column; join to wa_term_inventory.language.

name: top_sense_count
use: How many top-level senses the parse found in the definition text. 7,499 of 7,748 terms have exactly one; the maximum observed is 6, and 9 rows have zero.

name: stem_count
use: How many Hebrew verbal stems the parse broke out. Zero on 7,745 of 7,748 rows — only three terms ever received a stem breakdown, which matches the 13 rows in wa_meaning_stem.

name: has_causative_stem
use: 1 where the parsed definition evidences a causative stem (the term causes the inner state in another); set on 973 terms. Populated far more widely than stem_count, so it is detected from the definition text directly rather than from the stem breakdown.

name: has_domain_tags
use: Declared to mark parses carrying semantic domain tags, but 0 on every one of the 7,748 rows — domain tagging was designed and never performed, consistent with wa_meaning_sense.domain_tag being wholly NULL.

name: parsed_at
use: When the definition was parsed, ranging March to July 2026 across 309 distinct timestamps — unlike most tables in this group, the parse has been run incrementally as terms were added.

name: parse_version
use: Version of the parser that produced the row; uniformly '1.0.0', so every parse in the table came from one unrevised implementation.

name: parse_warnings
use: JSON array of issues the parser hit. Only one warning has ever been emitted — 'PROSE_ONLY', on 5,652 rows, meaning the definition had no numbered structure to parse. That is 73 per cent of the table, so for most terms the sense hierarchy below is a single prose blob rather than a real parse.

name: id
use: Surrogate key for the sense row.

name: parsed_meaning_id
use: The parse this sense belongs to, pointing to wa_meaning_parsed.id. 7,745 distinct parses, averaging just over two senses each.

name: level_code
use: The sense's own label from the source definition — '1' for a top-level sense, '1a' for its first subsense, '1a1' below that. This is the human-readable position in the hierarchy, and every parse has a '1' (7,739 rows).

name: level_depth
use: How deep the sense sits: 1 (8,050 rows), 2 (8,719) or 3 (356). Nesting never exceeds three levels in the current data.

name: parent_level_code
use: The level_code of the sense's parent, populated only for third-level senses (356 rows) — top and second-level senses leave it NULL rather than pointing upward, so the parent chain is reconstructed from level_code, not this column.

name: sense_text
use: The definition text of this sense — the substantive content of the row. 7,664 distinct values over 17,125 rows because many senses are short and common phrasings recur.

name: is_stem_label
use: Declared to mark a sense row that is really a Hebrew stem heading rather than a sense, but 0 on all 17,125 rows — never used.

name: stem_label
use: Declared to name the stem for a stem-heading row, but NULL on all 17,125 rows — never populated.

name: domain_tag
use: Declared to carry the sense's semantic domain, but NULL on all 17,125 rows — never populated, matching has_domain_tags being 0 throughout wa_meaning_parsed.

name: sort_order
use: Display position of the sense within its parse; 0 marks the first (7,745 rows, one per parse) and it rises to 34 for the most heavily subdivided definitions.

name: is_homonym
use: Declared to mark senses belonging to a distinct homonym of the lemma, but 0 on all 17,125 rows — homonym separation was never carried out.

name: id
use: Surrogate key for the stem row.

name: parsed_meaning_id
use: The parse the stem belongs to, pointing to wa_meaning_parsed.id. Only three parses are represented, with 6, 5 and 2 stems respectively.

name: stem_name
use: The Hebrew verbal stem named in the definition — Qal, Niphal, Piel, Hiphil, Hithpael and Hithpolel appear among the 13 rows.

name: stem_type
use: What the stem does to the verb's sense: 'base' (5), 'intensive' (4), 'causative' (3) and one 'piel_causative'. The last value straddles the naming scheme, mixing a stem name into what is otherwise a type vocabulary.

name: sense_count
use: How many senses the definition gives under this stem, from 0 to 9; four of the 13 rows have none.

name: top_sense_text
use: The leading sense the term carries in this stem (e.g. 'to be set apart, be consecrated'), which is the point of the breakdown — how the stem shifts the meaning. Distinct on all 13 rows.

name: obs_id
use: Surrogate primary key for the question, referenced by finding_question_link.question_id and wa_finding_catalogue_links.question_id.

name: question_code
use: The stable human-facing identifier for the question (for example 'C-001', 'WS-006'). Unique across the catalogue; the varied prefixes record the different families the catalogue accreted from.

name: section
use: The report section or tier the question belongs under, in long descriptive form (for example 'Section 3 — Annotated Verse Evidence', 'T3 — The Inner Faculties'). Free text with 27 variants and two competing naming schemes — 'Section N' and 'Tn' — running side by side.

name: source_word
use: The registry word whose analysis first raised the question, or 'Programme' where it is programme-wide rather than word-derived. Records the question's origin, not its scope.

name: source_registry_no
use: The word_registry id matching source_word, where the question came from a specific word study. Null on half the rows, which are programme-level.

name: question_text
use: The question itself as it is put to the analysis — the substantive content of the catalogue. Unique per row.

name: pattern_type
use: Tags a question as belonging to a mechanical pattern family, such as the VERSE_EVIDENCE_* flag prompts or lexical-discovery. 94% NULL, so it classifies only a small special-purpose subset.

name: scope
use: Whether the question applies programme-wide ('universal') or only within a corpus-specific study — the only exception is the twelve Leviticus terminology questions.

name: status
use: Lifecycle state: active, redundant_v1 (retired by the v2 restructure), superseded or dropped. Uncontrolled by any CHECK, and it duplicates and disagrees with the 'deleted' column.

name: deleted
use: Soft-delete marker; 243 rows are flagged, more than the 185 that status marks as non-active — the two columns are out of step and cannot both be trusted.

name: date_added
use: When the question entered the catalogue. Formats are inconsistent — some rows hold a compact 'YYYYMMDD' string, others full ISO-8601 UTC — so the column will not sort correctly as-is.

name: catalogue_version
use: The catalogue edition that introduced or last revised the question (for example 'v2.0', 'v2-2026-04-29', 'lev-v1'). Free text with no single versioning convention.

name: review_note
use: A dated prose note explaining a lifecycle decision — why a question was retired, migrated to an SD pointer, or dropped as fabricated. The audit trail for the catalogue's restructure.

name: tier
use: The evidence tier the question sits at, T1 through T7 plus T0. Null on 55% of rows, so tiering was applied only to the restructured portion of the catalogue.

name: component_code
use: The sub-component within the tier (for example 'T7.1', 'T4.2'), or in the Leviticus set a domain label like 'clean/unclean'. Two different coding conventions coexist in one column.

name: component_title
use: The human-readable name of the component_code (for example 'Lexical and Semantic Analysis'). Populated on the same rows as component_code.

name: prompt_seq
use: The order of the question within its tier and component, so a component's prompts are asked in sequence. Null wherever tier is null.

name: id
use: Surrogate key for the patch type, 1-20.

name: type_code
use: The patch type as it appears in a patch's metadata, e.g. 'CLUSTERING', 'DIMREVIEW', 'PREANALYSIS', 'PROSE'. Unique per row.

name: description
use: What the patch type does, e.g. 'Dimension Review per-registry patch — dimension + dominant_subject + optional Phase B revisions + registry stamp'. Populated for all 20.

name: session_b_status_exempt
use: Whether the patch type may be applied without meeting the Session B status gate: 1 for 18 types, 0 for only 2. The exemption is effectively the rule rather than the exception.

name: governing_instruction
use: Which instruction document defines the patch type, cited with the [current] token, e.g. 'wa-versecontext-instruction [current]' (7). The token means it resolves at read time rather than pinning a version.

name: schema_affected
use: Which tables the patch type writes to, as free text, e.g. 'verse_context, verse_context_group'. Not machine-checkable — one row reads 'varies (recovery-specific)' — so it documents intent rather than constraining anything.

name: deprecated
use: Whether the patch type is retired. 0 in all 20 rows — no patch type has ever been deprecated.

name: deprecation_note
use: Intended to explain a retirement, but NULL in all 20 rows, consistent with nothing having been deprecated.

name: created_at
use: When the type was registered. Three timestamps only — 15 rows from a single 2026-04-20 load — and inconsistently formatted, some with a Z suffix and some without.

name: last_modified
use: When the type was last changed. Only 4 rows have ever been modified, all in the same 2026-04-24 edit; the other 16 are NULL.

name: id
use: Surrogate primary key for the citation row.

name: prose_section_id
use: The prose section doing the citing. Only 25 distinct sections appear, so citation tracking was piloted on a small set and never rolled out.

name: cited_finding_id
use: The cited finding, referencing the legacy wa_session_b_findings table rather than the live finding store. Null on 45% of rows, which cite something other than a finding.

name: cited_qa_link_id
use: DEPRECATED (2026-08-29): the one live cross-reference INTO wa_finding_catalogue_links (FK to its id), found while retiring that table -- only 4 of 562 rows ever used it, all 4 resolve cleanly. Marked inactive to stop new citations routing through a deprecated link table; the 4 existing rows values are left untouched (their citation provenance is real historical data, not duplicated content -- no data loss). New citations should route through finding_id/cited_finding_id instead.

name: cited_sd_pointer_id
use: The cited Session D research pointer in wa_session_research_flags. Present on 38 rows.

name: cited_observation_seq
use: The cited observation as a textual sequence code (for example 'OBS-067-OBS-014'), used where the observation has no row to point at.

name: citation_form
use: The citation marker exactly as it appears in the prose — 'Q001', 'DIM-067-SD002', 'SP-067-018' and similar. This is the only column populated on every row, and the several distinct prefix families show the citation notation was never standardised.

name: paragraph_no
use: The paragraph of the prose section in which the citation occurs. 96% NULL, so the position of a citation within its section was almost never recorded.

name: delete_flagged
use: Soft-delete marker; no row has been flagged.

name: created_at
use: Insertion timestamp. Only five distinct values, confirming the table is the output of five batch runs on 27 and 28 April 2026.

name: id
use: Surrogate primary key for the prose-quality flag type.

name: flag_group
use: Free descriptive grouping label; 'PROSE_QUALITY' for every type seeded so far (escalation #833) -- a real taxonomy may emerge as more types do.

name: flag_code
use: The prose-quality issue this type names, e.g. 'Terminology change'. Unique.

name: description
use: What the type covers, in prose.

name: deprecated
use: Whether the code is retired: 0 for 25 codes, 1 for 4. Retired codes are kept rather than deleted so existing flag rows still resolve.

name: deprecation_note
use: Why a type was retired, if delete_flagged=1. Carried over unchanged from the pre-repurpose schema.

name: category
use: Legacy column, unused by the prose-quality vocabulary so far.

name: research_actions
use: Legacy column, unused by the prose-quality vocabulary so far.

name: id
use: Surrogate key for the rule, 1-59.

name: rule_id
use: The rule's citable identifier, e.g. 'GR-DATA-001', 'GR-CAD-001'. Unique, and the token used when instructions cite a rule.

name: category
use: What the rule governs: 'programme_orientation' 9, 'claude_code_directive' 8, 'process_discipline' 8, 'file_naming' 7 and ten others. Indexed but uncontrolled by CHECK.

name: subject
use: A one-line summary of the rule, e.g. 'Active terms filter — mandatory for all mti_terms queries'. Unique per rule and the practical way to scan the rule set.

name: rule_text
use: The rule's full normative text, often several hundred words. Populated for all 59 and the authoritative statement of each rule.

name: example
use: Intended to carry an illustrative example, but NULL in all 59 rows. It is superseded in practice by the plural 'examples' column, which is populated for 10 rows — two columns for one purpose, only one of them used.

name: applies_to
use: The rule's scope, e.g. 'all sessions, all phases' (28), 'Session B instruction' (3). Free text with no CHECK, so scope cannot be evaluated programmatically.

name: version
use: The rule's own version. DEFECT of format: two incompatible schemes coexist — underscore form ('2_1' 21, '1_1' 10) and dot form ('1.0' 15, '2.0' 7) — even though rule GR-FILE conventions in this same registry prescribe the underscore form.

name: added_date
use: When the rule entered the rule set, as a compact YYYYMMDD string (e.g. '20260414'). Note this is a different date format from every other timestamp column in the table.

name: last_modified
use: When the rule was last amended, ISO-8601 with Z. NULL in 23 rows, meaning those rules are unchanged since import.

name: obsolete
use: Whether the rule is retired: 34 live against 25 obsolete. Nearly half the rule set is superseded but retained so that existing citations still resolve.

name: obsolete_reason
use: Why the rule was retired, e.g. 'Absorbed into GR-OBS-001 2_0 as part of v2_8 consolidation'. Present for the 25 obsolete rules; the largest group (6 rules) was retired together when the RESEARCHER_DECISION format was replaced.

name: superseded_by
use: Which rule replaced this one, e.g. 'GR-RD-007 v1_0' (6). Inconsistent — some values name a rule with a version, others just a rule id — and it is a text pointer, not an FK to rule_id.

name: addendum_ref
use: Intended to point at a wa_addendum_registry item, but NULL in all 59 rows. The link is instead carried the other way, by wa_addendum_registry.rule_id.

name: source_document
use: Where the rule was imported from. Identical across all 59 rows ('wa-global-general-rules-v2_11-20260418.json') — the whole registry is one document's contents.

name: created_at
use: When the row was imported. Identical ('2026-04-20T15:55:51') across all 59 rows, confirming a single load.

name: rationale
use: Why the rule exists — typically explaining a failure mode it guards against. Present for only 13 of 59 rules, so most rules record their text without their reasoning.

name: application_notes
use: How to apply the rule in practice, including compliance tests; the longest field here, running to over 2,000 characters. Present for the same 13 rules that carry a rationale.

name: examples
use: Worked correct-and-wrong examples for the rule, e.g. 'Correct: v1_0, v2_7, v3_1. Wrong (SemVer-style dot): v2.7.' Present for 10 rules, and the column that the empty singular 'example' column was evidently meant to be.

name: id
use: Surrogate key for the assessment.

name: registry_id
use: The word_registry assessed. Only 112 and 182 were ever recorded.

name: file_id
use: The wa_file_index row for the word. Legacy linkage — file_index is no longer joined through.

name: relational_environment
use: Flag that the relational-environment dimension was found present. Set to 1 on both rows, so it never discriminated.

name: relational_environment_note
use: Prose finding on the relational environment, discussing which of the four rings are active for the word. The row's actual content.

name: spirit_soul_body
use: Flag that the spirit/soul/body dimension was found present. Set to 1 on both rows.

name: spirit_soul_body_note
use: Prose finding on where the word operates across spirit, soul and body, citing the verses that establish the boundary.

name: inner_operations
use: Flag that the inner-operations dimension was found present. Set to 1 on both rows.

name: inner_operations_note
use: Prose finding enumerating the inner operations the word is documented performing.

name: being
use: Flag that the being dimension was found present. Set to 1 on both rows.

name: being_note
use: Prose finding on the word as constitutive of identity or formed disposition.

name: raised_date
use: When the assessment was made — 2026-03-27 and 2026-03-28.

name: session_b_instruction
use: The instruction version the assessment was made under; a different one for each of the two rows.

name: id
use: Surrogate key for the finding.

name: finding_id
use: The human-readable finding code, unique across the table (for example '062-CHAR-001', 'SYN-INTRA-117-007'). Two visibly different code conventions coexist, one per-registry and one synthesis-scoped.

name: registry_id
use: The word_registry the finding belongs to. Coverage is very uneven — registry 30 alone holds 378 of the 2,883.

name: file_id
use: The wa_file_index row for the word; NULL on 325 findings. Legacy linkage — file_index is no longer joined through.

name: finding_type
use: The kind of finding, 40 distinct values led by OBSERVATION (1,343) and THEOLOGICAL_NOTE (445). Uncontrolled vocabulary, and 40 types across 2,883 rows indicates the taxonomy grew ad hoc.

name: finding
use: The finding text itself — the table's payload. One row holds an empty string.

name: anchor_verses
use: The verses the finding rests on, as a free-text list. NULL on 1,451 findings and an em dash on others, so half the store is not verse-anchored in this field.

name: raised_date
use: When the finding was raised; the timestamps cluster into large same-second batches, indicating bulk patch loads rather than individual capture.

name: session_b_instruction
use: The instruction document the finding was raised under, 17 distinct versions — useful for judging which findings predate a method change.

name: pass_ref
use: Which analysis pass produced the finding, recorded as a number 1 to 6 or similar; NULL on 363 rows. Uncontrolled vocabulary.

name: study_segment
use: The T-tier segment the finding sits under (T7.1, T0.3 and so on), under the retired tier scheme; NULL or empty on a large minority.

name: delete_flag
use: Soft-delete marker, set on 264 findings — the fabricated-finding drop of 2026-06-11.

name: obsolete_reason
use: Why a finding was retired. Effectively one value on 264 rows: dropped per the catalogue restructure of 2026-06-11 as a fabricated or templated DROP-family finding that was never validated. This is the record of the layer's known quality failure.

name: obsolete_date
use: When the finding was retired; 2,618 rows are NULL and 264 share the single timestamp of the June drop.

name: superseded_by_id
use: Wholly NULL — the supersession chain was never used.

name: related_finding_id
use: Pointer to a related finding; populated on only 8 rows, so effectively unused.

name: resolution_note
use: How the finding was disposed of, present on about 300 rows; mixes genuine resolutions with pasted tier-completion status lines, so it is not a clean field.

name: thin_evidence
use: Intended marker for weakly evidenced findings. Zero on all 2,883 rows — never once set, so it evidences nothing.

name: status
use: The finding's lifecycle state: resolved_qa (1,601), pending (983), routed_cluster (221), set_aside_non_evidenced and others. Uncontrolled vocabulary; the 983 still pending were never worked through.

name: term_id
use: Foreign key to mti_terms, ON DELETE SET NULL. Wholly NULL across all 2,883 rows — no finding here was ever bound to a term, which is why these findings cannot be reached through the term model.

name: synthesis_outcome
use: The synthesis verdict on the finding. NULL on 2,547 rows and the single value 'D' on the remaining 336, so it records no distinction.

name: tiers_engaged
use: Which T-tiers the finding draws on, as a comma-separated list; 56 combinations across the 336 synthesis rows. Free text, not a link.

name: structural_relationship
use: How the finding's elements relate: constitutive, enabling, parallel, sequential, causal, or N/A. Populated only on the synthesis rows. Uncontrolled vocabulary.

name: session_c_chapter
use: Which Session C chapter the finding was routed to. Uncontrolled and inconsistent — the same chapter appears as 'Ch2', 'Ch2 — How It Works' and 'Ch2 — How it works', so it cannot be grouped on reliably.

name: sd_pointer_ref
use: Reference to a Session D pointer. Populated on only 78 rows and largely holding the literal 'NONE' with a completion note appended, so it carries almost no pointers.

name: cluster_link
use: The M-code cluster the finding was matched to; NULL on 846 rows.

name: cluster_link_basis
use: How the cluster link was made: translit (1,548), strongs+translit (423), or strongs (66). Worth noting that most links rest on transliteration matching alone, which is the weakest of the three. Uncontrolled vocabulary.

name: id
use: Surrogate primary key; the range to 727 against 715 rows shows a few flags were hard-deleted.

name: registry_id
use: FK to word_registry — the study word the flag was raised on. 98 distinct registries carry flags, so flagging is concentrated on a minority of the ~215 words.

name: file_id
use: FK to the legacy wa_file_index for the source word-study file; NULL on over half the rows.

name: flag_code
use: The kind of flag: chiefly 'SD_POINTER' (357, a pointer to the abandoned Session D workstream), 'SB_FINDING' (203), 'VERSE_EVIDENCE_BREADTH_NOTE' (52) and 'BOUNDARY_DECISION_PENDING' (46), across 21 distinct codes. Convention only, no CHECK.

name: flag_label
use: The flag's unique label. Two generations coexist: a terse code form ('062-SD002') and a full sentence used as the label ('spoudē (G4710) operates across 11 distinct inner-being roles in 12 NT verses'), so the column is both an identifier and a headline.

name: strongs_reference
use: The Strong's number the flag concerns, where it is term-specific; NULL on two-thirds of rows.

name: cross_registry_id
use: A second word_registry the flag also implicates — the mechanism for recording that an observation spans two study words.

name: priority
use: 'MEDIUM' (496), 'HIGH' (165) or 'LOW' (34), plus 20 rows using an unrelated scale ('normal', 'advisory') — evidence of an uncontrolled vocabulary drifting across campaigns.

name: session_target
use: Where the flag is routed. Meaning-wise there are three targets, but they are spelled seven ways ('D'/'Session D', 'B'/'Session B', 'Researcher'/'researcher'), so filtering on this column requires normalisation. The 447 rows routed to Session D point at a workstream that was abandoned.

name: description
use: The substance of the flag — the observation, pointer or pending decision in prose. Required and unique on every row.

name: session_raised
use: Free-text record of the session or document that raised the flag, ranging from a bare 'B' to a full filename. No structure is enforced.

name: raised_date
use: The date raised, in inconsistent formats — some full ISO timestamps ('2026-04-30T07:56:14Z'), some bare dates ('2026-04-12') — so ordering requires normalisation.

name: resolved
use: 1 = closed (200 rows) versus 0 = open (515). The queue is 72% unresolved.

name: resolved_date
use: Date of closure; only 7 distinct values, so resolution happened in a few bulk sweeps rather than individually. Mixed date/timestamp formats as with raised_date.

name: resolved_note
use: Why the flag was closed — mostly bulk rationales such as 'Set aside non-evidenced 2026-06-01: no linkage route' (72 rows) or directive-driven routing to a cluster.

name: cluster_link
use: The M-code cluster(s) the flag belongs to, as a comma-separated string ('M04,M05') rather than a junction — so it cannot be joined to the cluster table without splitting. NULL on 318 rows.

name: cluster_link_basis
use: How the cluster link was inferred: 'translit' (258), 'strongs+translit' (117), 'strongs' (11), plus two one-off values. It usefully records that most cluster attributions here rest on transliteration matching rather than on Strong's identity.

name: id
use: Surrogate key for the term-in-registry record; referenced as term_inv_id by the related-words, root-family, flag and meaning-parse tables.

name: file_id
use: Foreign key to wa_file_index.id, the legacy per-registry file record this term was ingested under. wa_file_index is legacy and should not be joined through — use word_registry_fk on this table instead.

name: language
use: Source language of the term: Hebrew (5,423), Greek (2,231), Aramaic (190). Uncontrolled vocabulary, but unlike lexicon it does classify Aramaic properly.

name: term_id
use: The term's working identifier, normally the Strong's number. Not uniformly so: 17 rows use a descriptive fallback such as 'alupos_G_unconfirmed' where no Strong's was settled, so the column is a term key rather than a strict Strong's field.

name: strongs_number
use: The term's Strong's number, H/G plus four zero-padded digits. Null on 9 rows, and some rows carry a placeholder such as 'NO STRONG-135-metameleia' instead of a real number.

name: transliteration
use: Romanised lemma, declared NOT NULL but with rows holding only whitespace; never to be cited without the gloss.

name: step_search_gloss
use: The gloss as returned by STEP when the term was found — the source-of-record English sense, preserved unedited.

name: word_analysis_gloss
use: The gloss as it appears in STEP's word-analysis view. Nearly identical in cardinality to step_search_gloss (2,871 vs 2,873 distinct), so the two rarely disagree; holding both records that STEP exposes the gloss in two places.

name: occurrence_count
use: Corpus occurrence count for the term per STEP, up to 10,284. Null on 20 rows, and 0 is a real value for terms with no attested occurrence.

name: occurrence_count_qualifier
use: Caveat on the occurrence count where it is not exact — chiefly 'about' (636 rows) for an approximate figure. The remaining values ('image', 'to transform', a note on an Aramaic equivalent) are not qualifiers at all but stray content in the wrong column.

name: meaning
use: The term's full definition text, carrying STEP's numbered sense hierarchy. Populated on only 87 of 7,844 rows — the meaning text for the rest lives in the wa_meaning_parsed/wa_meaning_sense structure instead, so this column is a near-abandoned raw store.

name: meaning_numbered
use: Intended to hold the numbered form of the meaning, populated on only 96 rows and incoherent: values include real numbered definitions but also bare '0' and '1' (84 rows between them) and the string 'False'. Declared purpose is not borne out by the contents.

name: also_spelled
use: Records an alternative spelling or a Hebrew/Aramaic equivalent of the term, always with its gloss and Strong's (e.g. chi.lah H2427B). Present on only 18 rows.

name: lsj_entry
use: The Liddell-Scott-Jones classical Greek lexicon entry for the term, held raw. Present on 2,221 rows, though some of those are empty strings; it supplies classical-usage evidence that STEP's gloss does not.

name: testament
use: Which testament the term occurs in: overwhelmingly 'OT_only' (5,609) or 'NT_only' (2,213). Vocabulary is not enforced and has drifted — 7 rows say 'NT' and 3 say 'OT' where the _only forms were meant, and just one row is marked 'both'.

name: causative_form_present
use: 1 where the term has an explicit causative grammatical form (Hiphil/Piel in Hebrew, a stated causative sense in Greek), which bears on whether it describes causing an inner state in another. Set on 215 rows.

name: last_changed
use: Timestamp of the last write to the row, March to July 2026. Format is inconsistent — early rows use a space-separated form, later rows ISO-8601 with a T separator.

name: short_def_mounce
use: Mounce's concise definition for the term, a second lexical opinion beside the STEP gloss. Present on 2,214 rows, some of them empty strings.

name: parsed_meaning_id
use: Points at the term's row in wa_meaning_parsed, giving the structured form of its definition. Populated on 7,743 rows and near-unique, i.e. the parse is one-to-one with the term. Note the reciprocal FK also exists (wa_meaning_parsed.term_inv_id), so the link is held twice.

name: delete_flagged
use: Soft-delete marker; 713 of 7,844 rows are flagged out. Far less aggressive than the equivalent on mti_terms, where the majority is flagged — the two tables' live populations therefore do not correspond.

name: evidential_status
use: How much further research the term's evidence needs: 'research_not_required' (106) or 'pending_further_research' (49). Set on only 155 rows, all of them from the M29 remap of a legacy status scheme — the column was never rolled out to the wider inventory.

name: retention_note
use: Free-text reason a term was kept despite thin or doubtful evidence, e.g. zero verses but retained per default. Set on the same 155 rows as evidential_status, and 102 of those are just the mechanical M29 remap note rather than a researcher judgement.

name: term_owner_type
use: The core ownership marker: OWNER (3,996) means this registry is the term's canonical home with live verses and processed Verse Context; XREF (3,380) means a cross-reference copy whose verses are delete-flagged and whose context derives from the OWNER. Null on 468 rows, which are therefore unresolved for ownership.

name: term_introduction_source
use: Declared to record where a term was introduced from, but NULL on all 7,844 rows — never populated.

name: term_introduction_rationale
use: Declared to record why a term was introduced, but NULL on all 7,844 rows — never populated.

name: term_introduction_date
use: Declared to record when a term was introduced, but NULL on all 7,844 rows — never populated.

name: word_registry_fk
use: Direct foreign key to the owning English word in word_registry, spanning 195 registries. Fully populated with no nulls, and the sanctioned bypass around the legacy wa_file_index join — prefer this to file_id.

name: term_inv_id
use: The flagged inventory term, half of the composite primary key with flag_id, pointing to wa_term_inventory.id. 883 distinct terms, most carrying one or two flags.

name: flag_id
use: The flag type applied, pointing to phase2_flag_types.id. Spread fairly evenly across the vocabulary, led by 2 CAUSATIVE_OF_INNER_STATE (208), 16 SEMANTIC_RANGE_BREADTH (199), 1 GOD_AS_SUBJECT (196) and 3 SOMATIC_INNER_LINK (168).

name: description
use: Free-text elaboration of why the flag applies to this particular term, e.g. the named bodily organ behind a somatic flag. Present on only 17 of 1,570 rows — the bulk-patched majority carries no explanation.

name: source
use: What raised the flag: 'bulk_patch' on 1,092 rows, with only 17 rows attributed to named Session B passes. Null on 461 rows, which have no provenance at all.

name: raised_date
use: When the flag was raised. Just two values: a single timestamp for the whole 2026-03-19 bulk patch, and 2026-04-11 for the 17 Session B rows; null on 461 rows.

name: delete_flagged
use: Soft-delete marker; exactly one row of 1,570 has been retracted.

name: obsolete_reason

name: id
use: Surrogate key for the related-word row.

name: term_inv_id
use: The inventory term the relation hangs off, pointing to wa_term_inventory.id and cascading on its deletion. Around 7,151 distinct terms appear in the sample, i.e. nearly the whole inventory carries related words, averaging well over a dozen apiece.

name: gloss
use: English sense of the related lemma — the readable identifier for the relation, since the related word is not itself an inventory row.

name: transliteration
use: Romanised form of the related lemma; read alongside the gloss, never alone.

name: strongs_number
use: Strong's number of the related lemma, H/G plus four zero-padded digits. Null on a small fraction (528 of 34,641 sampled), where STEP named a related word without resolving it to a Strong's.

name: relationship_note
use: Free-text account of how the two lemmas relate. Almost never used — in the sample only 105 of 34,641 rows carry one, and 103 of those are the provenance stamp 'STEP relatedNos' rather than a substantive relation; only a couple are hand-written etymological notes.

name: delete_flagged
use: Soft-delete marker, 0 throughout the sample: no related-word link has been retracted, so this bulk import has never been pruned.

name: id
use: Surrogate key for the root-family membership row.

name: term_inv_id
use: The inventory term being assigned to a root, pointing to wa_term_inventory.id and cascading on its deletion. 2,860 distinct terms over 2,861 rows, so a term belongs to one root family and effectively never two.

name: root_code
use: The root family's identifier — the grouping key. Coding is not consistent: some codes are bare romanised roots (CHARAH), some are language-prefixed (HEB-tov), and one is the single character 'Ō'. 964 codes over 2,861 rows means many families have only one or two members.

name: root_language
use: Language of the root: Hebrew (1,442), Greek (784), one Aramaic. Null on 634 rows, which are therefore assigned to a root with no language recorded.

name: root_gloss
use: English sense of the root itself (e.g. 'burn/anger' for CHARAH), giving the meaning the family shares. Null on the same 634 rows as root_language, and some rows hold an empty string.

name: note
use: Provenance for the assignment. 2,188 of the 2,234 populated rows are the same stamp — backfilled 2026-04-09 from wa_term_related_words clustering — so the great majority of this table is derived from STEP's related-word data, not from etymological judgement. name: delete_flagged
use: Soft-delete marker; only 24 of 2,861 memberships have been retracted.

name: id

name: file_id

name: term_inv_id
use: FK to wa_term_inventory — the per-registry term entry (OWNER or XREF copy) this occurrence belongs to.

name: term_id

name: transliteration

name: testament
use: 'OT' or 'NT', denormalised from the book.

name: reference
use: The verse reference in programme form; the string key that pairs with verse_id.

name: verse_text
use: The ESV verse text, denormalised per occurrence and therefore stored many times over. Inconsistent with verse.verse_text: some rows carry the reference prefix and some do not.

name: last_changed
use: Timestamp of the last write to the row, spanning 2026-03-16 to 2026-07-13 — the widest window in the layer, reflecting this table's age.

name: book_id
use: Canonical book number, FK to books; NULL on a small number of rows.

name: chapter
