name: verse_num
use: Verse number, denormalised from the reference.

name: translation
use: 'ESV' on every row — the programme uses one translation, so this column distinguishes nothing.

name: note
use: Almost entirely empty; the only value present is 'master-index-backfill-2026', marking the rows touched when verse_id was backfilled from the master verse table.

name: claude_output
use: 100% NULL across all 247,046 rows. Declared to hold AI output on the record but never used — raw AI output goes through JSON patches instead.

name: created_at
use: ISO-8601 row creation timestamp; NULL on about a fifth of rows, so it cannot be relied on for age.

name: updated_at
use: ISO-8601 timestamp of the last bulk update; only 22 distinct values, all clustering on a handful of batch runs — it records campaigns, not per-row edits.

name: target_word
use: The English study word this occurrence was pulled for. Empty strings occur alongside NULLs.

name: span_strong_match
use: 1 = the occurrence's Strong's tag was confirmed against the morphological span; it is 1 on 243,788 rows and NULL on 3,258 but never 0, so it is a confirmation marker where NULL means 'unverified', not a true boolean.

name: context_before
use: The verse text immediately preceding the term's span, giving local context without a re-read of the verse.

name: context_after
use: The verse text immediately following the term's span.

name: delete_flagged
use: 1 = soft-deleted (171,156 rows) versus 0 = live (75,890). The majority of this table is deleted — chiefly XREF copies, whose verses are delete-flagged by design — so no read is safe without filtering.

name: mti_term_id
use: The Strong's-level term (mti_terms); one of the bypass FKs that should be used in preference to routing through wa_file_index.

name: morph_code
use: The morphology tag for the term's span, backfilled onto this table; NULL on roughly three-quarters of rows and only 867 distinct values against verse_morphology's thousands — a partial copy, so verse_morphology remains the authority.

name: stem
use: The Hebrew verbal stem for the span, backfilled and even more sparsely populated than morph_code; empty strings occur alongside NULLs.

name: word_registry_fk
use: Direct link to the owning word_registry entry — the bypass FK that replaces joining through wa_file_index; NULL on only a handful of rows.

name: verse_id
use: Link to the master verse table, backfilled after the fact. NULL on roughly 7% of rows, and those unlinked rows are exactly what verse_evidence_orphan records as unbindable — the layer's main known integrity gap.

name: analysis_marker
use: Stamp of the reading run that analysed this occurrence, e.g. 'Ecc-1-poetic-lexical-20260703'. It also carries the diagnostic value 'VERSE_NOT_IN_MASTER', which records occurrences whose reference has no counterpart in the verse table.

name: incorporated_in
use: Where the occurrence's reading was written up, e.g. a chapter/section code ('ECC-01-A') or a method label ('chapter-driven'); populated on a small minority of rows.

name: verse_span_id
use: Link to the specific word span in verse_span_index, tying the occurrence to its morphology. NULL on about three-quarters of rows, so span resolution is far from complete.

name: id
use: Surrogate primary key.

name: verse_id
use: Despite the name this is a FK to wa_verse_records.id (the term-in-verse occurrence), not to verse.id — a genuine naming hazard when joining. Distinct on every sampled row.

name: term_inv_id
use: FK to wa_term_inventory — the term entry the occurrence is linked to; cascades on delete.

name: step_subgloss_code
use: The Strong's code of the specific STEP sub-gloss matched for this occurrence, which may be finer-grained than the record's own term_id.

name: step_subgloss_label
use: The human-readable STEP sub-gloss text matched (e.g. 'zealot'). Values include leading whitespace (' Havens'), so the field is not trimmed.

name: span_strong_match
use: 1 on 237,269 rows and NULL on 262, never 0 — as in wa_verse_records, a span-confirmation marker rather than a boolean.

name: target_word
use: The English study word this link was created for; empty strings occur.

name: created_at
use: ISO-8601 creation timestamp, spanning 2026-03-23 to 2026-07-13.

name: id
use: Surrogate key for the value, 1-39. Also the self-referential FK target for superseded_by_member_id.

name: set_id
use: Which wa_vocab_set the value belongs to. Set 1 (the dimension labels) is the largest with 11 members; sets range from 3 to 11 members each.

name: value
use: The permitted value as it should be stored in the governed column, e.g. '01 — Emotion — Positive', '03 — Cognition', '0'. Unique within its set. Note the dimension labels embed a number and em-dashes in the value itself, so any column storing them must match that formatting exactly.

name: label
use: A short readable gloss for the value, e.g. 'Described — substantive synthesis finding'. Sparse — present in only 12 of 39 rows — so most values have no gloss.

name: description
use: What the value means in use, e.g. 'Automated classifier weak match — starting hypothesis, pending review'. Present for 27 of 39 rows, the inverse coverage of the label column.

name: sort_order
use: Display order of the value within its set, 1 upward. Populated for all rows with default 0, though no row actually holds 0.

name: deprecated
use: Whether the value is retired. 0 in all 39 rows — no vocabulary value has ever been retired.

name: deprecation_note
use: Intended to explain a value's retirement, but NULL in all 39 rows, consistent with nothing having been deprecated.

name: superseded_by_member_id
use: A self-referential FK intended to point at the value that replaced this one. NULL in all 39 rows — the supersession mechanism was built and never used.

name: introduced_at
use: Intended to record when the value entered its set, but NULL in all 39 rows — declared and never populated. created_at serves this purpose instead.

name: created_at
use: When the value row was written. Two loads only, matching the parent sets: 27 values on 2026-04-20 and 12 on 2026-04-30.

name: last_modified
use: When the value was last changed. NULL in all 39 rows — no value has ever been amended.

name: id
use: Surrogate key for the vocabulary set, 1-8, and the parent of wa_vocab_member.set_id.

name: set_code
use: The set's handle, e.g. 'DIMENSION_LABEL', 'DOMINANT_SUBJECT', 'stage2c_structural_relationship'. Unique, though the naming is inconsistent — the five older sets are UPPER_CASE and the three added on 2026-04-30 are lower_case.

name: name
use: The set's readable title, e.g. 'Dimension Review — 11 Inner-Being Dimensions'. Populated for all 8.

name: description
use: What the vocabulary means and how its values are to be used, often summarising the values inline. The fullest statement of each set's semantics.

name: governing_doc
use: Which instruction ratified the vocabulary, e.g. 'wa-dimensionreview-instruction [current] §7.7'. Reveals that five of the eight sets belong to the retired dimension-review layer.

name: applies_to
use: The DB column the vocabulary constrains, e.g. 'wa_dimension_index.dimension'. Telling: most targets are on legacy tables, and one row admits '(logged in observations, not a DB column)' — that set governs no column at all.

name: deprecated
use: Whether the set is retired. 0 in all 8 rows, even though the dimension-review sets govern a layer that is no longer live.

name: deprecation_note
use: Intended to explain a retirement, but NULL in all 8 rows.

name: created_at
use: When the set was declared. Two loads only: five sets on 2026-04-20 and three on 2026-04-30, and the two batches format the timestamp differently (one with a Z suffix, one without).

name: last_modified
use: When the set was last changed. NULL in all 8 rows — no vocabulary has ever been amended since declaration.

name: id
use: Registry number for the word, 1-222, and the identifier used everywhere as 'registry N'. It is duplicated exactly by the 'no' column.

name: no
use: A second registry number, 1-222. It is identical to id in every one of the 222 rows, so it is wholly redundant with the primary key and carries no independent information.

name: word
use: The English inner-life word the registry entry is about, e.g. 'zeal'. 222 rows hold only 218 distinct words — deadness, resentment, transformation and vulnerability each appear twice, so the word is not a unique key.

name: source_list
use: Where the word came from into the programme. Dominated by four conventional buckets ('Missing Inner Being Words' 86, 'High Confidence' 75, 'Programme Addition' 28, 'Low Confidence / Inferred' 24) but uncontrolled — later rows carry free-text provenance such as an extraction date, so the vocabulary is convention only.

name: category_hint
use: An early, loose semantic hint for the word ('Anthropology', 'Affective/Emotional', 'Sin & Vice'). Largely abandoned: NULL in 186 of 222 rows, and its 22 values overlap inconsistently with the 'dimensions' column.

name: phase1_input_file
use: The file or engine run that supplied the word's Phase 1 data, mostly of the form 'RUN-20260318_150513-NEW_WORD'. Sparse — NULL in 175 of 222 rows — so it documents only a minority of Phase 1 loads.

name: phase1_status
use: How far Phase 1 discovery has got for the word: 'Complete' 176, 'Excluded' 42, with 2 each 'In Progress' and 'Pending'. No CHECK enforces this set, so the four values are convention.

name: phase1_output_file
use: Comma-separated list of the JSON patch filenames Phase 1 produced for the word. NULL in 190 of 222 rows, and it stores a list in a single text field rather than one row per file.

name: phase2_datasets
use: DEFECT: the column is declared REAL but holds a mix of types — 26 rows store a numeric dataset count (1.0, 2.0, 3.0) while 4 rows store a filename string such as 'FrameworkB-SessionB-Registry111-Mercy-20260326.docx'. The declared type contradicts the contents and the column conflates a count with a file pointer.

name: notes
use: Free-text working notes on the word, in practice dominated by appended engine audit lines of the form '[AUDIT 2026-07-11] result=REVIEW terms=123 verses=5712 run_id=...'. Populated for 220 of 222 rows; it is an append log inside a text field, not a structured record.

name: automation_eligible
use: Whether the engine may process the word automatically: 1 for 193 words, 0 for 29. Boolean-by-convention as an INTEGER with default 1; no CHECK constrains it.

name: last_automation_run
use: DEFECT: the name and its sibling timestamps imply a run time, but 193 of 222 rows hold the literal string 'AUDITED' instead of a date, with only a handful of rows carrying an actual 2026-03-18 timestamp. The column now mixes a status token with a datetime and cannot be read as either.

name: automation_run_id
use: The engine run that last touched the word, e.g. 'RUN-20260325_053955-AUDIT_WORD'. Near-fully populated (1 NULL) and mostly unique per word, though 27 words still point at the single bulk run RUN-20260318_134133-BULK_GAP_FILL.

name: phase1_term_count
use: How many Hebrew/Greek terms Phase 1 found for the word. 27 rows sit at 0, which corresponds to the words never extracted or excluded.

name: phase1_verse_count
use: How many verse records Phase 1 found for the word, ranging from 0 to the hundreds. 28 rows are 0, marking words with no verse evidence gathered.

name: strongs_list
use: A JSON array of the word's Strong's numbers with their occurrence counts, e.g. [{"strong": "G0225", "count": 90}, ...]. It is a denormalised snapshot of what the term tables hold authoritatively; 27 rows carry an empty array '[]'.

name: description
use: The researcher's prose account of what the word names in the inner life — several hundred characters of substantive definition. Populated for 212 of 222 rows and one of the genuinely content-bearing fields here.

name: origin
use: Whether the word came from the original ~214-word list ('original_list', 185) or was added later ('programme_addition', 27). Two values, uncontrolled by CHECK; NULL in 10 rows.

name: dimensions
use: The word's inner-being dimension label, e.g. 'Affective/Emotional' (48), 'Moral/Conscience' (34), 'Character/Disposition' (19). 15 values with no CHECK behind them, NULL in 34 rows; it belongs to the retired dimension layer.

name: inference_note
use: The researcher's reasoning where a modern English word has no direct biblical equivalent — typically explaining that the concept is ABSENT as a single term and how Scripture handles it instead. Deliberately sparse (35 of 222 rows), attaching only to the inferred/absent words.

name: session_b_status
use: How far Session B has got for the word: 'Verse Context Reset' 160, 'Analysis Complete' 12, 'Ready for Analysis' 5, NULL 45. Uncontrolled vocabulary, and only three of the six documented statuses actually occur in the data.

name: cluster_assignment
use: The word's C-code dimension cluster, C01-C22 (C22 16, C02 14, C08/C10/C19 11 each). DEFECT worth noting: its DEFAULT is the double-quoted literal "unassigned", which SQLite accepts as a string only by falling back from identifier parsing — a fragile declaration.

name: sb_classification
use: The word's spirit/soul/body placement from an abandoned classification pass. use: 'stable' (fixed filename, overwritten/archived on regenerate) or 'dated' (versioned filename per report)

name: archive_dir
use: where a superseded 'stable'-scheme report is archived

name: step
use: the report-producing step this section belongs to

name: ordinal
use: the section's position in the report

name: section_key
use: the section's stable identifier

name: heading
use: the markdown heading text rendered for this section

name: toc_label
use: a shorter label for the table of contents, if different from the heading

name: include
use: 1 if this section is actually rendered

name: step
use: the report-producing step this CSV export belongs to

name: table_name
use: the table (or, if virtual=1, the named derived result set) this CSV covers

name: join_note
use: plain-language description of a multi-table join, if the export isn't a single verbatim table

name: virtual
use: 1 if table_name is a computed/derived name rather than a literal live table

name: id
use: surrogate key

name: config_version
use: the app's config_version string at the time of this load

name: seed_hash
use: a hash of the seed content, for change detection

name: loaded_at
use: when this load happened

name: validated
use: 1 if this load passed validation

name: key
use: the setting's dotted key, e.g. 'governance.reports_must_persist'

name: value
use: the setting's value, JSON-encoded

name: use
use: what this setting controls and why

name: database
use: which physical database table_name refers to -- part of the primary key (iba.db and bible_research.db share table names, e.g. 'passage', for different tables; escalations #653/#680 widened cfg_table/cfg_write_grant the same way, this closes the same gap for cfg_unique). Config differentiation only.

name: concept_key
use: short kebab/snake-case identifier, e.g. 'verse_primacy'

name: chapter
use: which chapter (0-6) this concept belongs to, per prose_section_type.chapter_no in bible_research.db -- no longer FK'd to a table; cfg_prose_chapter removed 2026-08-27, escalation #918

name: section_hint
use: which section(s) within the chapter, in plain language (prose sections aren't independently keyed yet)

name: description
use: a short gloss of the concept, for discoverability -- the prose itself remains authoritative for the full definition

name: source
use: provenance -- which prior rule/decision this concept pointer replaces or derives from

name: added_at
use: when this concept was registered

name: id
use: serial PK, 4-digit display; continues from escalations_old's max (735) so ids stay unambiguous across the cutover

name: version
use: current version number for this id -- count of its escalation_history rows; the NNNN-NN display format is id+version, not a stored key

name: run_id
use: restored 2026-08-20 (v1 dropped it, broke dispatch, rolled back -- BUILD.md §152/§153). Set for a DISPATCHER-TIED item (a real run.py pause, correlates back to the run being resumed) or a synthetic MANUAL-<timestamp> for a manual item. NULL for neither.

name: source
use: what triggered the item: script name | module | issue area. Immutable after Raise.

name: at_step
use: pipeline reference, only set if code-generated/run-error. Immutable after Raise.

name: type
use: differentiates the kind of item

name: short_description
use: label/title -- what this item is about. IMMUTABLE after Raise (plan v3 §3) -- a wrong title is corrected by raising a new item with state=supersede on the old one (plan v3 §4), never edited in place.

name: context
use: what must be done or the error message, plus links to external documents. Cumulative: an Update's input is the increment, appended onto the current value (plan v3 §2).

name: comment
use: additional information for the assigned party. Cumulative, same rule as context.

name: tried
use: the corrective action taken -- REQUIRED when next_action_assigned_to=Claude and a prior corrective action failed (plan v3 §6/v2 §6).

name: state
use: current status -- raised at Raise; mostly logic-derived on Update per the auto-state rules (plan v3 §3), some values either-party-settable (on-hold/in-progress/closed).

name: next_action
use: what's expected of the current reader (incoming) / what the next reader should do (outgoing) -- TWO vocabularies share this column: dispatcher-tied (approve/reject/revise/hold/noted, unchanged) and manual (ready_for_approval/approved/reject/revise/noted/review) -- see lib/escalation.py module docstring, 2026-08-20.

name: next_action_assigned_to
use: Claude | Researcher

name: originator
use: who created the latest escalation_history row -- auto-populated, replaces `answered_by`. Not caller-supplied.

name: resolution
use: what was actually done -- REQUIRED when next_action=approved (validity check, plan v3 §3).

name: raised_at
use: first creation datetime -- set once, immutable

name: answered_at
use: mirrors the latest escalation_history row's timestamp

name: id
use: surrogate PK, row order = write order

name: escalation_id
use: which item this snapshot belongs to

name: version
use: this item's version number at the time of this snapshot -- matches escalation.version at the moment this row was the latest

name: run_id
use: snapshot of escalation.run_id (constant per item)

name: source
use: delta: NULL after v1 unless source is corrected (it normally never changes after creation) -- was wrongly NOT NULL under the retired full-snapshot design

name: at_step
use: snapshot of escalation.at_step at this version

name: type
use: delta: NULL after v1 unless type is corrected -- was wrongly NOT NULL under the retired full-snapshot design

name: short_description
use: delta: NULL after v1 unless the title is explicitly corrected (rare, exceptional) -- was wrongly NOT NULL under the retired full-snapshot design

name: context
use: delta: the raw increment THIS version added, NULL if this version didn't touch it -- same correction as comment, above

name: comment
use: delta: the raw increment THIS version added, NULL if this version didn't touch it -- was wrongly 'full cumulative text' under the retired full-snapshot design (that design wiped 2026-08-20, researcher: 'the cumulative is only in escalation')

name: tried
use: snapshot of escalation.tried at this version

name: state
use: snapshot of escalation.state at this version

name: next_action
use: snapshot of escalation.next_action at this version

name: next_action_assigned_to
use: snapshot of escalation.next_action_assigned_to at this version

name: originator
use: who created THIS specific snapshot -- the real per-update author, never overwritten by a later row (this is the fix for #715's loss)

name: resolution
use: snapshot of escalation.resolution at this version

name: raised_at
use: delta, structural: only ever set at v1 (the item's true creation time; never changes) -- was wrongly NOT NULL every version under the retired full-snapshot design

name: answered_at
use: THIS row's own write timestamp -- the real per-update datetime

name: priority
use: evaluation order within its shape, ascending, first match wins

name: shape
use: 'manual' or 'dispatcher' -- which vocabulary/function this rule belongs to

name: next_action
use: which next_action this rule matches, or NULL to match any

name: condition_key
use: named condition the code evaluates (escalation-rebuild-design-v1 sec2.4) -- a fixed small vocabulary, not a general expression language

name: resulting_status_key
use: substring matched against cfg_status_flow.set_by (entity=escalation) to resolve the target status

name: notes
use: why this rule exists / provenance

name: active
use: inactive rows are skipped during evaluation

name: action
use: 'raise', or a next_action value -- which transaction this requirement applies to

name: field
use: the escalation column that must be filled in

name: condition_key
use: 'always', or a named condition gating when the requirement applies

name: message
use: shown to the caller when the requirement is violated

name: active
use: inactive rows are skipped

name: check_kind
use: which comparison lib/escalation.py._check_requirements runs: 'field_required' (value must be truthy -- the original, only, implicit behaviour before this column existed), 'not_raised_with_content' (value must NOT be 'raised'), 'exists' (value, if set, must reference a real escalation id), 'not_self' (value, if set, must not equal the item's own id). Added 2026-08-21, register v9 D14/D25/D26.

name: crash_escalation_reviewed
use: 1 once this module's crash-recovery behaviour (does a mid-write failure roll back cleanly, does it record itself) has been genuinely reviewed, not bulk-defaulted (D3, register v9). 0 = not yet reviewed.

name: crash_escalation_note
use: The genuine finding from that review -- what actually happens if this module's write crashes mid-transaction. NULL until crash_escalation_reviewed=1.

name: key
use: the setting's key, e.g. 'passage.quality_report_path' -- kept identical to the prior cfg_setting key text so no caller string changes, only the table read from

name: value
use: JSON-encoded value, same convention as cfg_setting.value

name: use
use: what the setting controls and why

name: inactive
use: soft-disable flag, same convention as cfg_setting

name: resolution_kind
use: decision_required or self_correctable (cfg_enum resolution_kind) -- required at Raise, escalation #798/#799. decision_required is terminal and routes to design; self_correctable is fixed directly by Claude, no approval gate. Mutable in one direction only: self_correctable -> decision_required via escalate_to_decision(), never the reverse.

name: resolution_kind
use: per-version snapshot of escalation.resolution_kind at that version.

name: inactive
use: a column that is declared but dead (never populated, or the concept it served is retired) is marked inactive=1 here -- symmetric with cfg_table.inactive (escalation #678), not DB-enforced (nothing stops a write to it), but makes the fact config-known and queryable. Escalation #833, researcher: 'this may not be DB enforceable, but at least it sets the config that the column is not used.'

name: id
use: Own PK. The value written into a covered target row's version column.

name: target_table
use: Which table this entry describes a change against.

name: target_id
use: Which row of target_table this entry describes. Not a hard FK -- deliberately generic across tables.

name: change_type
use: insert / change / delete, CHECK-constrained. See escalation #836 proposal sec 6 for the mapping against every existing write operation.

name: change_datetime
use: When the change was applied (system time, ISO-8601 UTC) -- not the underlying event's own real-world date.

name: change_source
use: File name, if driven from an input file; otherwise the originating script/module identifier.

name: change_reason
use: Free text, not enum-constrained. Population rule: flag type for a flag-driven change; otherwise the change's own source reference.

name: changed_by
use: Who/what executed the change. Distinct from prose_section.author (authorial voice) and .approved_by (accountable sign-off).

name: status
use: change_proposed / change_applied / declined, CHECK-constrained. Default change_applied.

name: payload
use: Gzip-compressed JSON. The prior content this change overwrote or removed -- never the resulting content. NULL for insert events and migration-baseline rows.

name: updated_at
use: When this row was last written, touched on every write path including session_a_replace -- the gap that motivated this table's versioning rebuild (escalation #836). created_at is reserved for true original-creation time only.

name: version
use: Pointer to record_change_log.id, same meaning as prose_section.version (escalation #836). This table has never carried a version concept before.

name: updated_at
use: Touched on every write (escalation #836). created_at reserved for true creation time only.

name: key
use: the setting's key, e.g. 'prose.book_stage_map' -- kept identical to the pre-#829 cfg_setting key text so no caller string changes, only the table read from

name: value
use: JSON-encoded value, same convention as cfg_setting.value

name: use
use: what the setting controls and why

name: inactive
use: soft-disable flag, same convention as cfg_setting

name: prose_section_id
use: Identifies the citing prose section, with an FK to prose_section.

name: verse_reference
use: The cited verse, as a loose reference string matching wa_verse_records.reference's own format (e.g. 'Ps 32:1') -- not an FK (see cfg_table.use for why).

name: link_type
use: Qualifies the relationship, defaulting to 'discusses' -- same convention as prose_section_finding_link/prose_section_dimension_link.

name: created_at
use: Insertion timestamp, defaulting to datetime('now').

name: path
use: Project-root-relative path (POSIX slashes) of the file. Primary key -- one row per file.

name: category
use: Coarse classification (iba/session/script/cluster/discovery/workflow/investigation/patch/report/doc/log/directive/code/export/import/backup/other) -- computed by lib/manifest.py:classify_category() from the path's leading folder segments, project-naming FACT not cfg_setting. folder_purpose.manifest_category (escalation #971) will become the primary source once built, this classifier the fallback for any folder not yet registered.

name: file_type
use: Finer-grained type within category, e.g. 'iba-lib', 'analysis-patch' -- lib/manifest.py:classify_type().

name: currency
use: current/archived/cross-reference/historical/backup/other -- lib/manifest.py:compute_currency(), same fallback relationship to folder_purpose.

name: archived
use: 1 iff currency='archived' (path contains an archive/ segment) -- redundant with currency, kept for cheap WHERE archived=1 filtering.

name: registry
use: word_registry id extracted from the filename, when the naming pattern carries one -- NULL for files not tied to a specific word registry.

name: word
use: English word extracted from the filename, when present.

name: cluster
use: M-code cluster extracted from the filename, when present.

name: vcb_batch
use: Verse-context-batch number extracted from the filename, when present -- legacy Session B naming.

name: version
use: The -v{n} version suffix extracted from the filename, when present.

name: date
use: Date extracted from the filename (compact or hyphenated), when present.

name: ext
use: File extension, lowercase, including the leading dot.

name: size_bytes
use: File size in bytes at scan time.

name: modified_at
use: The file's own filesystem mtime, UTC ISO-8601.

name: scanned_at
use: When this row was written by manifest.rebuild() -- identical across every row from the same run; a full rebuild replaces the table's contents rather than updating in place.

name: folder_path
use: Project-root-relative folder prefix, POSIX slashes, no trailing slash. Primary key -- one row per governed folder, seeded from a full census of every directory in the tree.

name: top_level_root
use: First path segment (or '(repo root)' for the root itself) -- cheap grouping/filter key.

name: depth
use: Path segment count; 0 = repo root.

name: parent_path
use: This folder's immediate parent's folder_path.

name: direct_file_count
use: Files directly in this folder, not counting subfolders -- refreshed by the manifest-validate method (Method A) on every manifest rebuild, never hand-edited.

name: recursive_file_count
use: Files in this folder and everything under it -- Method A-refreshed.

name: direct_subfolder_count
use: Immediate child folders -- Method A-refreshed.

name: top_ext_direct
use: Up to 5 file extensions by count among this folder's direct files -- Method A-refreshed.

name: last_modified_direct
use: Latest mtime among this folder's direct files, UTC ISO-8601 -- Method A-refreshed.

name: governed_by_setting
use: Which cfg_setting key(s) already point at this exact folder path (semicolon-joined if more than one) -- refreshed by the configmaint cross-check (Method B), config-side truth, distinct from Method A's disk-side truth because a setting can change with no file moving.

name: manifest_category
use: What file_manifest.category a file in this folder should get once folder_purpose becomes the manifest's primary classification source (escalation #971 Part D) -- NULL until set.

name: manifest_currency
use: Same, for file_manifest.currency -- NULL until set.

name: type
use: archive|operations|results (cfg_enum folder_purpose_type) -- the researcher-facing coarse classification, hand-set via FolderPurpose.ps1 (Method C), never touched by Methods A/B.

name: status
use: authoritative|mixed|reallocate|stale|deleted (cfg_enum folder_purpose_status) -- 'deleted' is set by Method A when a folder no longer exists on disk (soft delete, row never removed); the other four values are hand-set via Method C.

name: usage_description
use: Free-text description of what this folder is actually for, in the cfg_table.use/cfg_column.use style, scoped to a folder -- hand-set via Method C.

name: added_at
use: When this row was first created.

name: last_reviewed_at
use: When type/status/usage_description were last confirmed accurate via Method C -- lets Method A/B flag a row whose judgement fields haven't been reviewed since its disk facts changed.

name: characteristic_id
use: FK -> characteristic.id. Added 2026-08-29 during the cluster_finding migration -- retains that tables structural link rather than dropping it.

name: cluster_subgroup_id
use: FK -> cluster_subgroup.id. Added 2026-08-29 during the cluster_finding migration -- retains that tables structural link rather than dropping it.

name: vcg_scope
use: Verse-context-group identifier(s), sometimes semicolon-joined multiples (e.g. M03-C-VCG-02). Added 2026-08-29 during the cluster_finding migration -- no prior equivalent on finding.

name: notes
use: Free-text notes. Added 2026-08-29 during the cluster_finding migration (45%% populated there) -- no prior free-text field on finding.
